conventions.convention: Balanced sutured manifolds have no closed components, equal total positive and negative Euler characteristics, and an annular suture meeting every boundary component. Connectedness and nonemptiness are not required.

The meridionally sutured exterior has two oppositely oriented meridional sutures. Alexander grading is half the relative Chern-class evaluation on the specified Seifert surface, with the stated meridional trivialization and the usual S3 sign.
The knot Floer groups used for detection have integer coefficients. A group isomorphic to Z is the hypothesis; a mod-two rank calculation is not substituted for it.
Integral disk counts use a coherent orientation system; diagram comparisons transport its class. The zero-curve diagram has one empty generator and zero differential.
Horizontal and separating-annulus decompositions give graded tensor complexes. Their integral homology formula includes Künneth Tor terms; the plain homology tensor formula is asserted over fields.
Genus detection is stated for knots in S3. The general-Y fibering implication additionally requires an irreducible knot complement and retains the actual Seifert surface and its class.
The detection results assume full AC. Conditional countable-choice selection results do not weaken the imported analytic framework's assumptions.

load_bearing.statement: Assume full AC. For the stated null-homologous knot, genus-g Seifert surface and surface-adapted admissible diagram, the top Alexander generator correspondence identifies the knot and cut sutured disk-count differentials. The stated horizontal and essential separating-annulus hypotheses give their respective chain decomposition formulas.

Assume full AC. For a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented Y with irreducible complement and genus-g Seifert surface F, an integral grading-g knot Floer group isomorphic to Z implies that the exterior cut along F is a product sutured manifold.

The Alexander grading is half the relative Chern-class evaluation on F using the meridional trivialization; the integral grading-i knot Floer group is the direct sum of the corresponding integral sutured Spin-c summands.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a smooth oriented knot K in S3, its Seifert genus is the maximum integer Alexander grading with nonzero integral hat knot Floer homology.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For the stated null-homologous knot with irreducible complement and genus-g Seifert surface F, an integral grading-g knot Floer group isomorphic to Z implies fibering with fiber F.
Assume full AC. A null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented Y whose complement fibers with connected Seifert fiber F of genus g has integral grading-g knot Floer group isomorphic to Z.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. The quotient P=S3/I* is a closed connected oriented integral homology sphere with universal cover S3 and nontrivial fundamental group I* of order 120.

concerns.concern: The Definition starts with an arbitrary balanced sutured manifold and says: 'Two such fields are homologous when, outside some open ball in int M, they are homotopic'. Balanced manifolds here may be disconnected. On two disjoint product balls, take fields v, w, z with the fixed boundary values: w differs from v by one local Hopf modification in the first component, and z differs from w by one in the second. Then v is related to w and w to z, but v is not related to z: a single ball lies in one component, leaving a nontrivial relative Hopf difference in the other. Thus the stated relation is not transitive and does not define homology classes at this scope. The empty balanced manifold also has no ball witnessing reflexivity. The original [Juhász 2006, §4](https://msp.org/agt/2006/6-3/agt-v6-n3-p16-s.pdf) explicitly assumes connectedness before this definition. The actual knot exteriors are connected, but the general definition needs adjudication.

The Definition defines periodic domains and admissibility in its first paragraph, then repeats both definitions after the d=0 paragraph; Whitney disks, Maslov index and coherent orientations are also repeated. These repetitions add no mathematical content and obscure the single chain-level convention.

alerts.finding: The Statement begins 'For an actual weakly admissible balanced sutured diagram on a surface with boundary, the integral disk complex exists for each specified coherent orientation class' without a choice hypothesis. However F5 explicitly imports the analytic framework 'in the classical full-Choice setting of F4', and Proof 3.16 says 'This invocation is in the full-Choice background F4' and that a Countable-Choice application requires a separately justified specialization. The public Statement therefore omits an essential hypothesis of its supplied proof. Batch 96's actual uses retain full AC, so this is a supplier-interface finding rather than a demonstrated failure of those consumers.
